parameters.content:
## Gemini Image Studio

Serves its own HTML interface straight from a webhook: drop in up to two reference images, pick a mode, and Google Gemini returns a finished image. No bucket, no CDN, no frontend to deploy.

### How it works

1. A GET on the webhook returns a single-page studio interface, generated inside n8n from the values in **Settings (UI)**.
2. The page downscales each upload in the browser, then POSTs the mode, the options and the images back to the same URL.
3. **Validate & build prompt** checks the request, decodes the images into binary and assembles the prompt for the chosen mode. Bad input gets a 400 with a readable reason.
4. One of three Gemini nodes runs depending on how many images arrived: text to image, a single-image edit, or a space + logo composite.
5. The result comes back as a data URL with its prompt and metadata, so the page can show it, download it, or feed it in again as the next reference.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Attach a Google Gemini (PaLM) API credential to the three `Gemini:` nodes.
- [ ] Set an image-capable model in **Settings (generator)** (`gemini_model`).
- [ ] Adjust the title, subtitle and upload limits in **Settings (UI)**.
- [ ] Activate the workflow, then open the production webhook URL in a browser.

### Customization

Six preset modes live in **Validate & build prompt**: reword their prompts, or add your own and mirror the key in **Build studio page**. Output ratios and upload limits sit in those same two nodes.

## Read before running

The three `Gemini:` nodes need a **Google Gemini (PaLM) API** credential, and `gemini_model` must name a model that can both generate and edit images.

n8n's **test** webhook serves only one request, and loading the page consumes it, so Generate will fail there. Use the production URL.

## One webhook, two methods

GET serves the interface, POST generates the image. The node exposes one output per HTTP method, so no router node is needed.

## Serve the studio interface

Builds the entire page - HTML, CSS and JS - inside n8n and returns it as text/html.

## Validate the request and route it

Decodes the uploaded images into binary, builds the prompt, and answers 400 on bad input instead of throwing.

## Generate with Gemini

One node per image count. Each retries twice, then sends hard failures out through its error output.

## Return the image or the error

Packs the result as a data URL, or turns a Gemini failure into a 502 the interface can display.
